sample.title: The Technology Transforming China’s Factories | Bloomberg Primer
sample.description:
China is both the world’s largest CO2 emitter and clean technology exporter. It’s responsible for almost a third of global carbon emissions while dominating electric vehicles, batteries and solar panels. In 2020, President Xi Jinping announced national goals tied to peak emissions and carbon neutrality. Recently, Beijing has rolled out programs to shift Chinese factories toward a greener future. One tactic is called the zero-carbon industrial park, an effort to run manufacturing hubs on renewable power. Can the world’s largest exporter move to a greener era of mass production?

sample.description:
After more than a decade of development and an estimated $1 billion-plus investment, Grand Theft Auto 6 is shaping up to be one of the biggest video game launches ever. Analysts project billions of dollars in sales, while Take-Two investors will be watching to see whether the highly anticipated game can live up to sky-high expectations. Its impact could reach far beyond gaming, with ripple effects for creators, food delivery, streaming, music and other forms of entertainment. CNBC’s Julia Boorstin examines the business behind GTA 6, the risks facing Rockstar Games and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, and what the release could mean for the wider entertainment industry.

sample.title: The rise, reinvention and uncertain future of Nvidia without Jensen Huang
sample.description:
In the early months of the AI boom, after OpenAI launched ChatGPT in November 2022, Nvidia was on the precipice of historic growth. Jensen Huang told CNBC he’d like to keep running the company for “three or four decades,” as long as “I feel that I’m making a real contribution to the company.”

Less than four years later, Jensen Huang is out, and we’re taking a look back at our interviews with the Nvidia co-founder and other company executives as the chipmaker enters this next critical chapter.

Watch the full story in related video.

sample.title: Will A Democratic Congress Ease U.S. Tariffs On Canada?
sample.description:
The Blue Wave that swept the U.S. in the 2026 midterm elections could be a boon for Canadian stocks. The newly elected Democrat-controlled Congress is expected to put pressure on Trump to soften or eliminate tariffs imposed by his administration on Canada. The rolling back of those heavy trade taxes stands to benefit the metals, auto parts, and lumber industries, among others, in the Great White North. Liz Napolitano reports.

sample.description:

The BBC’s Environment Correspondent Jonah Fisher speaks to experts and swimmers to find out what went wrong at Britain’s worst wild swimming spot.
